messages.subject_clean: [OGRUG] Ottawa Gatineau R User Group (R-UG-Ottawa) meeting
messages.body_plain:
WHERE: FTX 135,  University of Ottawa

http://www.uottawa.ca/maps/

will show you where this is.

WHEN: 3:30-5:30, Tuesda May 24, 2011

WHY: To allow R users in Ottawa/Gatineau to get reacquainted. Please be willing to
introduce yourself and tell what you do and your interest in R.

There will be a "How do I .... in R" session. At least 2 such queries have been suggested.
If you have one, or an interesting issue/solution, send email to me or the R-UG-Ottawa
list. I will aim to post them before the meeting.

Also I will give a short account of the explosion in activity in the Google Summer of Code
effort by R this year.

Time permitting, we may wish to discuss how the R-UG could assist local R users more.

Please pass this along to anyone you believe should be interested.

There is no charge for this event.

Best, JN

messages.subject: [OGRUG] Two R queries for Tuesday's meeting
messages.subject_clean: [OGRUG] Two R queries for Tuesday's meeting
messages.body_plain:
A reminder of time and place below.

Query 1: to create a frequency matrix of 32 cells (5 binary variables), and then export
that matrix into a text file that can be read by a package e.g. as a .dat file.


Query 2: If I create a new.env(), how do I find the right objects. In particular, if I am
running a process such as integration, optimization or ODE solution, can I have an
environment to keep a table of the evaluated functions separately. THat is

    Calling program  --->    optimizer  ----> objective function
     parameters/data         parameters/data     parameters/data
    sepearate env.                              function results matrix in separate env.

where the separate env. is not seen by the optimizer code?

Other queries. Post to the list before Tues afternoon.

messages.subject: [OGRUG] Report on May 24 meeting
messages.body_plain:
While we had only a small group (8) at the meeting, discussion was lively and some minor
problems were resolved.

There was quite a lot of interest in the projects R is mentoring for the Google Summer of
Code. This year we have 15. There is a brief outline of the projects linked directly from
the main www.r-project.org page.

There were two pre-announced R coding questions.

David Joubert had an SPSS data file that he wanted to bring into R to either use in
creating a 5 dimensional frequency array or else convert to a numerical (rather than
character) raw data file of binary information on 5 symptom variables for 500 cases.

The foreign package can read the data into a data frame, but the binary variables are of
class factor. After the meeting a bit of playing showed that as.numeric() will convert
these to numbers (1, 2) and write.csv will write them in a form that is easily changed in
a spreadsheet to the form needed by some specialized software. It should in fact be
possible to avoid the last step by appropriate parameters to write.csv.

John Nash illustrated a concern for those working on optimization, differential equations
or quadrature when it is desired to record every function evaluation of a multivariate
function e.g., the objective in optimization. The issue is to avoid passing such
information through the optimizer, which may be compiled code and difficult to access.
While it should be possible to use environments, there seemed to be a general view that
this tended to be more tricky than anyone liked. However, we were able in a small example
to set a global object f.save to NULL, then use rbind inside the function to append the
vector c(f, x_vector). It was agreed this was NOT a good idea for inclusion in a package,
but likely the most straightforward tool for experimentation.

This lead to a discussion of the merits of using return() to end R functions, and a brief
attempt to test the speed of use of return(x) versus just ending with the evaluation of x
using the microbenchmark package. This was inconclusive for the simple example tried.

We hope to have a similar event in the Autumn with more problems pre-announced.

John Nash

messages.subject: [OGRUG] R-UG-Ottawa Digest, Vol 15, Issue 3
messages.body_plain:
Hello John,
Thank you for hosting the R-User meeting on Tuesday. I found it interesting.
However, I was a bit disappointed with the turn out. I thought that there
would be more people with an interest in R here. You can count of me as an
active member from now on.
In the fall, at one of the meetings, I would be happy to give a 20 minute
talk on "Spatial classes and their use in R". Also I have done a fair bit of
work with the packages 'plyr' and 'data.table' for the
manipulation/massaging of data in R (if anybody would be interested in
learning about these things I could give a short presentation?).
Also is there a way I can communicated with any of the people attending the
meeting by e-mail? Did anybody collect the e-mail addresses of the people
there?
Again thanks for your work in organizing things. Have a productive "Google
Summer of Code".
Regards,
John Lewis
